item.title: Re: Drooling Path 3
item.content:encoded: Yeah, you’re right. What if I cut the James parts entirely and abbreviated them at the beginning of part 4? So little happens that I feel like that wouldn’t be much trouble. Then I could use the extra space to go into more detail about Dr. Scott’s fears, goals, and expectations regarding the hotel, and maybe delve some more into the whole thing with his wife and 4068.

item.title: Re: Drooling Path 3
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
[-] Close

The Conrad aspects of this feel…weird. For a story about Conrad going on a journey to the Atherton Hotel, it very much feels like the actual journey is secondary and all of the story is just kinda covering him thinking about how he feels about the journey as a whole and planning out various aspects of it. This isn’t necessarily bad per se but it makes it feel insubstantial on it’s own since there’s not really a lot happening; and it also feels like it’s a poor setup to a fourth part of this since we don’t really get a feel for what will happen at the Hotel. Specifically: whilst Conrad dwells on the maybes a lot, the lack of knowledge (or even plausible theories) for what he might find at the Hotel means that his arrival there doesn’t inspire emotions within me. I’m not worried Conrad will die, or excited for the revelation he’ll find or really much of anything because I genuinely have no idea what he’ll find there. And so without there being much interesting happening on his journey either, it feels…underwhelming.

The James aspects have similar issues: setting up that James might end up in danger and his increasing investigations into the CD he stole is cool but it doesn’t get time to go anywhere. He never listens to the CD, and so it just feels like this whole section is a holding pattern as we wait for something to happen.

I think on it’s own either one of these stories feeling very interstitial like this, like this is a quiet break before the cool action, could work; but neither feeling like they advance this in an interesting way leads to this piece just feeling…too much like it’s padding out the story more. I wouldn’t think this was as much of an issue if the first parts in the story had been more exciting but since this brings the series up to ~9.5k words as a whole, I’m left feeling…drained and not really looking forward to the continuation a tonne?

I guess if I was to summarise, it’d be that it feels like this needs to setup the stakes more: some indication of how bad can the events go; not just in a vague ‘Conrad presumes he could die’ way but in a precise way where we can see the shape of the danger at least somewhat. Perhaps the best way to do this would be the addition of a third perspective, this time from either a neutral or antagonistic force, perhaps a narrator hinting at what awaits in the Atherton hotel, or perhaps a view from like, the hotel owner preparing some devious trap?

item.title: Drooling Path 3
item.content:encoded:
I wrote two tales a long time ago about an unhinged researcher's quest to solve the mysteries behind SCP-058, SCP-1981, and certain other SCPs yet to be revealed. Now, part three is finally complete(ish) and I am ready for some feedback.

My biggest concerns are:

  • Is there too much boring stuff unrelated to the plot?
  • Is the pacing wonky?
  • Is the ending too abrupt/does it not leave a strong enough impression?

It's the tab called "Drooling Path 3", naturally:

http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/kothardarastrix
